parsed.explanation: The combined regime splits: this state/province sits in a documented low-risk group — no facility ban, no care ban, vetoes blocking restrictive bills, municipal and executive nondiscrimination protections, marriage recognition — but the visitor cannot avoid the national layer. Federal passport rules force birth-sex markers, the 24 Feb 2025 cable routes document-discrepant applicants into refusal and potential lifetime fraud findings, foreign trans citizens have been detained, and federal custody documents severe abuse. Entry screening is a universal-exposure measure every trans visitor carries; the state offers no remedy against it. Threat-framing from national institutions ('radical gender ideology' counterterrorism prioritisation) raises outing consequences. Net: elevated risk mitigated by the state's genuinely tolerant operative environment, held below Reduced-Risk anchors by unavoidable federal exposure.

entry_documents.exposure: National passports/visas process only M/F per birth sex; Feb 2025 cable instructs refusal on document discrepancy and considers lifetime fraud ineligibility; foreign trans citizens detained over visa issues; allied governments issued travel advisories.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports remain valid until expiration; litigation against passport policy ongoing; legal-aid FAQ helps travellers prepare documents.
entry_documents.interaction: Entry exposure is federal and unavoidable regardless of the state's tolerant rules; airport screening can out travellers before any state protection applies.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections bureau policies described as conversion practices for trans inmates (hair cutting, hormone removal); immigration custody: forced labour, beatings, solitary, severe sexual abuse reported by trans men.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any immigration or criminal detention places the visitor in a federal custody regime with documented anti-trans harm; state courts offer no control.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National order bars trans access to federally funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity; 20+ states ban such access in government buildings, 4 with criminal exposure.
federal_state_facilities.protection: This state/province has no facility ban, no restrictive sex definition, no drag restriction; visitor may use congruent facilities statewide.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Federal buildings/programs inside the state still apply the federal rule; state facilities are governed by the state's non-ban.

care_services.exposure: Two major hospital systems paused under-18 gender-affirming pharmacologic care in Jan 2026 under federal funding pressure; federal orders target youth care; subpoenas for minors' hospital records.
care_services.protection: No state ban on minor or adult care; governor vetoed ban and insurance restriction twice; adult care and insurance coverage protected; state joined coalition against federal declaration.
care_services.interaction: A travelling minor may find pharmacologic care unavailable despite no state ban — the constraint is federal money, not state law.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National justice memoranda frame 'radical gender ideology' alongside violent extremism; counterterrorism strategy prioritises 'radically pro-transgender' groups; state criminalised one restroom arrest elsewhere.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: State executive order (2019) bars gender-identity discrimination in state employment, contracting, services; city police stopped recording victim gender to avoid misgendering.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: State agencies and police operate under protective state orders, but federal framing raises stakes if a visitor enters federal contact.

minors_guardians.exposure: National orders label youth care 'mutilation'; teachers facilitating social transition face prosecution directives; hospital records subpoenaed; pharmacologic care paused at major systems; state licence/BC offer no X marker and restrictive name change.
minors_guardians.protection: No state minor-care ban; vetoes preserved access; gender-neutral parent options on birth certificates; adoption without regard to orientation.
minors_guardians.interaction: A guardian travelling with a trans minor faces federal records/school directives and paused care; state provides partial shelter only.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: No statewide gender-identity hate-crime protection; prosecutors sometimes charge via perceived sexual orientation; national bias data shows persistent anti-LGBT incidents.
street_violence_police_response.protection: Hate crimes punishable nationally; sexual orientation protected statewide since 1982; 33% of population covered by full local gender-identity ordinances; prison hormone access judicially guaranteed.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Local police response is uneven but generally neutral-to-protective; hate-crime recourse exists partly through the sexual-orientation route.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Remedies against federal passport/refusal rules unresolved in court; Jan 2026 care pause status unknown; licence marker documentation standard unstated; risk-assessment methodology unpublished.
remedies_unknowns.protection: State legal-risk assessment places the jurisdiction in its low-risk group; multistate coalition challenging federal health declaration ongoing.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Uncertainty is concentrated at the federal interface (entry, funding, litigation), not in state daily life.

anchor_checks.comparison: 0.35-A is a universal registration/exclusion regime with no remedy. Here entry-document exposure is comparably universal (binary markers, refusal cable, detentions of foreign trans citizens), but no systematic exclusion-from-entry regime is documented and state-level life is openly tolerant — materially above 0.35, not equal to it.

0.55-B's secondary screening, humiliation, discretionary refusal mirrors the federal entry layer here. This dossier adds documented custody abuse and state threat-framing (worse), but pairs it with a genuinely protective host state (better). Net: similar-to-slightly-above 0.55.

0.75-C's trained border officers and functioning tribunal remedies exceed what the federal record here documents (confiscated passports, stranded travellers, fraud findings). The state layer approaches 0.75, but the federal layer does not, so the combined regime sits below it.

0.65-A shows a brief stop, working national equality law, reliable judicial release — remedies functioning. Here state remedies function but the federal entry/custody exposures are heavier than 0.65-A's single incident; slightly below 0.65 fits.

parsed.synthesis: The operative regime the traveller encounters is a tolerant state embedded in a hostile federal framework. Within the state, documented features are protective or neutral: no facility ban, no care ban, twice-vetoed restrictive bills, municipal nondiscrimination ordinances covering a third of the population, recognised marriage, guaranteed prisoner hormone access. Daily life inside the state resembles a 0.70–0.75 jurisdiction. But entry is federal and unavoidable: every trans visitor carries binary-marker document exposure, the February 2025 cable creates a refusal/fraud pathway, foreign trans citizens have been detained, and if detention or immigration custody occurs, documented harms include forced labour, beatings, sexual abuse, and conversion-style prison policies — severity-4 outcomes with no state remedy. Federal threat-framing of 'radical gender ideology' raises the consequence profile of any federal contact. Universal federal exposure plus severe-but-lower-frequency custody harms, offset by a protective host state, yields ~0.60: elevated risk, safer than the national picture alone, below jurisdictions where the protective layer extends to the border.
